Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

compress noun

also hot compress, cold compress, warm compress, fomentation

classical

Hor. Serm. 1.1.82: assideat, fōmenta paret, medicum roget, of Horace’s friend at the bedside

fōmentum, fōmentī n.

noun, second declension

compress, warm application, fomentation

From foveō.

Other words

  • fōmenta calida / frīgida — warm / cold compresses

    also used · classical

Examples

  • fōmenta quoque calida sunt milium, sāl, harēna, quidlibet eōrum calfactum et in linteum conjectum

    warm compresses are millet, salt, sand, any of them heated and put in a clothCels. 2.17

  • Fōmentum calidum tibi in pectus impōnam.

    I’ll put a warm compress on your chest.composed

See also bathe, poultice, bruise, cold.

SourcesLewis & Short: fomentum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency has no entry for a compress.

Celsus (2.17) and Horace checked against the Perseus Latin texts.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
